newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan briefed on Tuesday's meeting between labour and employer groups on a code of conduct on informing and consulting workers in case of plant closures or restructuring. She said the ETUC was in favour of a review of current legislation on information and consultation but that the UNICE was not convinced of such a need.

Nolan said the social dialogue committee would report back to the Commission and meet on June 6. She also said the formal joint Presidency and Commission conclusions would be available in her office. Nolan also said Commissioner Padraig Flynn stressed the need for the issue to be pursued rapidly, and have results ready in time for the June Social Affairs Council. She said the Commission was hoping to bring forward its proposals on procedures of information and consultation at national level in the coming months.
Nolan briefed on Thursday's Social Affairs Council.

In answer to a question, spokesman Willy Helin said there were no divergence of views between Commissioners Karel van Miert and Commissioner Martin Bangemann on the issue of Spanish digital television legislation.
